newsitem.title: GERMANY: German retail coffee prices may have to rise - DKV.
newsitem.headline: German retail coffee prices may have to rise - DKV.

text.p: German coffee roasters are being squeezed amid higher raw material and dollar costs and low retail prices, a spokesman for the DKV coffee industry association said on Monday.
They might see a need to increase ex-plant prices to account for additional costs, he said in response to an enquiry by Reuters.
"Operational factors make price rises look necessary and it looks as if they could come, but the timing is uncertain," he said.
Arabica futures have risen strongly during the latest rally on anticipated tightness in the upcoming 1997/98 season and low consumer country stocks.
Prices have fallen since last Friday but bullish market fundamentals remain in place.
Outright prices of premium coffees for the German market have increased even more strongly than reflected on the futures exchange, the spokesman said.

Roaster Eduscho GmbH & Co KG last week raised the price of one product, but competitors Kraft Jacobs Suchard and Tchibo Frisch Roest-Kaffee GmbH, the number one and two in the market, said they had no immediate plans to follow suit.
A similar line was taken on Monday by Munich-based Alois Dallmayr Kaffee, with an eight percent market share, and at Hamburg's J.J. Darboven, which accounts for seven percent.
